plan: This is a second-price auction (I pay the second-highest bid if I win). In second-price auctions, bidding my true value is the dominant strategy - it maximizes expected profit regardless of others' bids. Bidding higher than value risks paying more than the item is worth if others bid between my value and my bid. Bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. My value is $42, so I should bid exactly $42.

This is a second-price auction where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy. If I bid exactly my value ($29), I win whenever the second-highest bid is below $29, paying only that second-highest bid, which guarantees non-negative profit. Bidding higher risks paying more than the item is worth if I win against a high second bid. Bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Since this is a single round with no repeated learning needed, truthful bidding is optimal.

This is a second-price auction where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy. Since I win and pay the second-highest bid if I have the highest bid, there's no incentive to bid above or below my true value of $48. Bidding exactly my value ensures I win whenever profitable (when my value exceeds others' bids) and never overpay (since I'd only pay what the second-highest bidder bid, which would be less than my value in a winning scenario).
